issues.issue: The headline DEPENDS ON D INIT covers two opposite outcomes. (gauss: SURVIVES, unit: SURVIVES, zero: VANISHES) is the pattern the paper's mechanism predicts: the gain is there with the described Gaussian D at both scales and absent with affinity-blind routing. (gauss: VANISHES, unit: VANISHES, zero: SURVIVES) is the opposite. Both get the same headline, which reads as a hedge against the paper in the first case and hides a two-scale failure of the described init in the second. SURVIVES as a bare horizon label also requires the control arm to survive, which is not what the paper claims.
issues.evidence: PREREG §7 Horizon label: 'if all three per-arm labels are equal → that label … Otherwise → DEPENDS ON D INIT (gauss: …, unit: …, zero: …)'. §5 defines tfps_zero as a control (uniformly random expert), not a TFPS configuration the paper describes.

issues.issue: The name of the Q3 horizon fallback label, DEPENDS ON D INIT, makes a causal claim about D that the rule does not test. The rule fires whenever the three per-arm labels disagree and are not all negative. Seed noise alone often causes that disagreement, even when all three arms have the same distribution (which the init probe suggests for unit vs zero, see the next issue). The label is therefore often the modal horizon outcome in cases where D has no effect. It can also contradict the Q2 labels printed beside it, for example Q2 EQUIVALENT for both contrasts next to Q3 DEPENDS ON D INIT. This does not make any verdict unreachable. It does make the label wrong as worded in many plausible cases.

issues.issue: tfps_gauss_unit is, at init, indistinguishable in routing from tfps_zero. Q2 for that contrast is therefore expected, though not guaranteed by construction, to give EQUIVALENT (if sd allows) or INCONCLUSIVE, with about 5% per side for rules 1-2 under a null. The prereg's stated init numbers for this arm are also off. Two exact facts follow from Cluster.py:61-68. (a) s_unit(z) = s_N01(z/sqrt(112)) for the same G, so the unit arm reaches the N(0,1) arm's init spread only if ||z|| grows about 10.6x (the s range of a random-subspace D is bounded near 0.14 at any scale; r2 sweep). (b) argmax s is scale-invariant, so at init arms 1 and 2 have the same argmax partition, and the Q2b noise-off unit model starts from the same deterministic routing as arm 1. The outcome stays open: training can grow z or rotate D through the KL term. This is not blocking, because Q2 asks whether the init matters in the released code, and 'no' is a legitimate answer. But a reader should know in advance that the unit arm is effectively a second random-routing control unless training sharpens s, and that the routing suffix will almost surely fire for it.

answers.q1_unit_vs_zero_routing: At init the two are not distinguishable. A is 0.2516/0.2505 for unit vs 0.2500 for zero, a gap of less than 1 noise-draw sd. The mean s range is 0.005/0.008 for unit vs 0 for zero. Q2(unit) is expected, not guaranteed, to come out EQUIVALENT or INCONCLUSIVE. It can differ only if training grows ||z|| by about 10x or the KL term rotates D. The routing suffix (A < 0.30) will almost surely fire for unit.
answers.q2_horizon_rule: Negative horizon labels are reachable, and including tfps_zero does not make them unreachable. Per-arm labels are strongly correlated because all three arms share the same baseline samples. With identical arms and no true gain, VANISHES (or worse) fires at the horizon level 0.86-0.96 at H=192 and 0.88-0.96 at H=336 for sd_T ≤ 0.006, close to the single-arm rate. Negatives become rare only when the zero arm is truly better (H=336, sd_T 0.012: 0.06), or when noise is large (H=336, sd_T 0.012: 0.18 vs single-arm 0.53). The real cost of the rule falls on SURVIVES, which needs unanimity (0.14-0.24 vs 0.51-0.61 for a single arm at sd_T 0.012), and on the over-frequent DEPENDS ON D INIT label (major issue above).

Q2 EQUIVALENT: 0.0094/0.0043 (n=5), 0.0142/0.0064 (n=10). SHRINKS: PatchTST 0.0140/0.0049, DLinear 0.0042/0.0057 (n=5). The 'no width floor' claim for REVERSED/VANISHES/SURVIVES/Q2 rules 1-2 is literally true. VANISHES needs U in [0, m) because REVERSED is checked first, a window of width m in d. Exceptions: the Q2 sub-label and Q2b floors (minor issues). For the DLinear contrast in the realistic unequal-sd case, the SHRINKS floor is σ_T < 0.011/2.199 = 0.0050 at H=192.

lenses.summary: No verdict family is settled or made unreachable by how the arms are built. The forward probe shows that tfps_gauss_unit routing at init matches tfps_zero (A 0.2516/0.2505 vs 0.2500; mean s range 0.005/0.008), because s_unit(z) = s_N01(z/√112). Q2(unit) is therefore expected, though not guaranteed, to come out EQUIVALENT or INCONCLUSIVE, and §5's init numbers for that arm should be corrected. The all-arms rule for negative Q3 labels does not make them unreachable: shared baselines keep the arm labels correlated (VANISHES at the horizon level 0.86-0.96 under a no-gain null). But DEPENDS ON D INIT fires 60-80% with identical arms, so it needs a neutral name (major, mechanical fix). The §7 reachability numbers are correct, except for the Q2 sub-label and Q2b paired floors.

issues.issue: Seed collision between eval-noise draws and the D generators. Eval draw k uses global seed 10000k+seed, so k=3 gives 30000+seed (the time-D generator seed) and k=4 gives 40000+seed (the frequency-D generator seed), for every seed. torch's CPU generator gives the same normal stream for the same seed whether global or dedicated, so the 'fresh' router noise in draws 3 and 4 is largely a shifted copy of the D initial values (G) of arms 1-2. Probe (torch 2.4.1 CPU, seed 2021): global manual_seed(32021) then randn(1536,4) equals randn(112,112) from Generator(32021) exactly (100% of entries); with one int64 draw first (what a DataLoader iterator consumes), 75% of entries equal G at a shift of 2. Effect on scores is probably negligible (each noise value is one of 12544 D entries), but draws 3 and 4 are not independent of arm 1/2's initialisation as the design assumes, and it is free to avoid.

issues.issue: The three-arm horizon rule's fallback label 'DEPENDS ON D INIT' fires often when D init makes no difference, so it asserts an effect no test has shown. Any disagreement among the per-arm labels produces it, for example SURVIVES/SURVIVES/SHRINKS from sampling noise or VANISHES/VANISHES/INCONCLUSIVE. Per-arm labels are thresholded and the arms are noisy, so three arms with identical true accuracy often disagree. At large TFPS seed sd this label, not INCONCLUSIVE, becomes the modal outcome.
issues.evidence: Monte Carlo (simulations key), all three arms with the same true mean. True gain = m: P(DEPENDS) = 0.09-0.13 even at sigma_T = 0.002 (rho 0; 0.04-0.06 at rho 0.9). It is 0.11-0.22 at sigma_T 0.005-0.01, and 0.73-0.77 at sigma_T 0.02 (rho 0). True gain = m/2: 0.55 at H=192 and 0.78 at H=336 at sigma_T 0.01 (rho 0). True gain = 0, H=336, sigma_T 0.02: 0.76. When D really matters (zero arm worse by min_B m_{H,B}), P(DEPENDS) = 0.97-0.99, so the label detects arm differences but does not distinguish them from noise.
issues.fix: Mechanical, inside owner decision 9 (negative labels still need every arm). Replace the fallback with: if every per-arm label is in {SURVIVES, INCONCLUSIVE}, or every one is in {REVERSED, VANISHES, SHRINKS, INCONCLUSIVE} with at least one INCONCLUSIVE, then INCONCLUSIVE (per-arm: ...). Otherwise `ARMS DISAGREE (gauss: ..., unit: ..., zero: ...)`, worded as 'D init changes the Q3 label', and add 'D-init effect on accuracy: see Q2' with the Q2 labels at that H. Keep the name DEPENDS ON D INIT only if at that H some Q2 contrast is GAUSS BETTER or ZERO BETTER. Add one sentence to §7 quoting the P(DEPENDS | identical arms) figures above.

issues.issue: There is no fallback if the FREEZE check yields a margin <= 0. The prereg admits this is possible: r2 fairness recalled DLinear H=336 = 0.481, which gives m_{336,DLinear} = -0.003 and makes DLinear the best baseline at H=336, so m_336 = -0.003. Then (a) Q2/Q2b EQUIVALENT and the ', smaller than m_H' sub-labels need a CI inside an empty interval: unreachable by construction. (b) The trigger condition 'Q2 90% hw >= m_H' is always true, so extension fires mechanically. (c) The Q3 rules quantify over 'both B' and 'some B', but §1 makes that B 'non-gating' without saying how the rules, the Bonferroni level or the trigger then treat it.
issues.evidence: PREREG §1 lines 28-31 (m_H = margin over best Table 1 baseline; 'If the checked m_{H,B} <= 0 ... non-gating'); §7 rules 1-4 (lines 202-208) and trigger (line 237) reference m_H and every (a,B) without exception.
issues.fix: Add to §1: (1) Q3 rules and the trigger range over gating B only. With one gating B, U is the one-sided 95% bound (no Bonferroni) and 'both'/'some' reduce to that B. With none, Q3 at that H is DESCRIPTIVE ONLY. (2) If the checked m_H <= 0, Q2/Q2b at that H use m_H := min over gating B of m_{H,B}; if none is gating, 0.005, stated as audit-chosen. (3) Non-gating pairs are excluded from T.

issues.issue: The horizon rule does not say what happens when one TFPS arm is BLOCKED. Literally, BLOCKED/SURVIVES/SURVIVES yields 'DEPENDS ON D INIT', which is wrong. A negative is impossible because BLOCKED is not in the negative set, even though the other arms may agree. A BLOCKED tfps_gauss (N(0,1), aux-dominated selection) is a realistic case.
issues.evidence: §6 lines 161-162 (Q3 for arm a BLOCKED if a or either baseline is); §7 lines 210-213 (horizon rule lists only REVERSED/VANISHES/SHRINKS as the negative set).
issues.fix: Add: if any TFPS arm is BLOCKED at H, the horizon label is `INCOMPLETE (<arm> BLOCKED; others: ...)`. It is neither negative nor positive, in line with owner decision 9's 'every TFPS arm'. If a baseline is BLOCKED, the horizon label is BLOCKED.

issues.issue: The extension trigger is close to mechanical but still leaves its inputs open: which TFPS checkpoint (released or pure-val-MSE), which baseline scores (lr-searched or published-lr), whether BLOCKED arms and non-gating pairs count, the df when an se is 0, and that m_{H,B} means the FREEZE-checked values.
issues.evidence: §7 lines 235-242: 'reads only per-seed primary scores and computes ... T = [any Q2 contrast with 90% hw >= m_H] OR [any (a, B) with hw_L + hw_U >= m_{H,B}]'.
issues.fix: State: T(H) = OR over a in {gauss, unit} of [t_{.95,nu}·se(a, zero) >= m_H], OR over non-BLOCKED a in {gauss, unit, zero} and gating B of [(t_{.95,nu} + t_{.975,nu})·se(a, B) >= m_{H,B}]. Here se and nu are Welch-Satterthwaite from released-selection primary scores and lr-searched baseline scores (n = 4 for an arm with one failure). Margins are the FREEZE-checked ones. If se = 0, the width is 0. Expected P(extend) at sigma_T 0.005 is 0.55-0.85 and at sigma_T >= 0.01 is ~1, driven mostly by DLinear at H=192 and Q2 at H=336; budget accordingly.

issues.issue: Two things in the qualifiers are undefined or asymmetric. 'If it does not hold there' (published lr) does not say what 'hold' means: does REVERSED -> VANISHES hold? In Q3 the SELECTION-SENSITIVE qualifier is attached only to negative horizon labels, while Q2 applies it to every label. Item-level 'same horizon label' is also undefined for parameterised labels (DEPENDS/ARMS DISAGREE with different per-arm contents).

issues.issue: Q2's gating Welch test ignores the pre-registered pairing: arms share non-D init, data order and noise stream by construction. If D has little effect, the within-seed correlation is high and Welch is conservative in both directions. Under rho = 0.9 the false GAUSS/ZERO BETTER rate is ~0.00 and EQUIVALENT power drops less than it would under independence (H=336, sigma 0.005: EQUIVALENT 0.68 vs 0.34 at rho 0). The effect is symmetric, so no verdict is biased. It costs power only and is already disclosed (paired reported, non-gating).

lenses.summary: Every number in the §7 reachability paragraph recomputes correctly for Q3. Bonferroni-on-U / IU-on-L brings the some-B negatives to <=5% (sim 3-4%). Both verdict directions are reachable for sigma_T <= ~0.01, and the extension trigger's type-I cost is under 0.5 pp. Three major issues, each with a mechanical fix. (1) The three-arm fallback 'DEPENDS ON D INIT' fires 9-79% when the arms are identical, so it asserts an untested D effect. Relabel it and route agree-or-inconclusive mixes to INCONCLUSIVE. (2) No fallback if the FREEZE check gives m <= 0: Q2 EQUIVALENT becomes unreachable and the trigger always fires. (3) A BLOCKED arm is unhandled in the horizon rule. Minor: trigger inputs, Q2 sub-label/Q2b thresholds, qualifier definitions.
